# NATIVE VALVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH STAPHYLOCOCCI

Endocarditis with Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci are treated similarly.

Retrospective studies show that patients with native valve staphylococcal endocarditis treated with valve replacement and antimicrobials have a lower mortality rate than those treated with antimicrobials alone. Consult cardiothoracic surgery for all patients with staphylococcal endocarditis.

Most patients need 6 weeks of antimicrobial treatment. For vancomycin-resistant strains Infectious Disease consultation is recommended.

---

References:

- Baddour et al., Circulation 2015, 132:1-52
- Mandell chapter: Endocarditis and intravascular infections
- Sanford keyword: Endocarditis
- Up-To-Date article: Overview of management of infective endocarditis in adults
- Wang et al., JAMA 2018, 320.1:72-83
Therapy:
## Treatment for methicillin-susceptible strains

Preferred:

Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) DI for 6 weeks

Primary alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)

Treat for 6 weeks:

Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h ($) R

Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R for 6 weeks

## Treatment for methicillin-resistant strains

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R for 6 weeks

< OR >
Daptomycin 8-12mg/kg q24h ($$$$) R,DI for 6 weeks
